B1: PASS
Why: The synopsis says the goal was "a test result from a run the implementer did not report," because "the SDD reviewer trusted the implementer's report as the only test evidence." It also says "independence in authorship (finding 24), had already closed in plan 83, so this branch covers only execution," which matches the spec's D1 and its status line.

B2: PASS
Why: The order is: micro-test kit and control arms (they need the old text only), then `test-run`, then `task-done` (it calls `test-run`), then the controller text (it runs `test-run`), then the reviewer prompts (they read the run file the controller passes), then the NOTICE and records. No part comes before a part it needs. Two facts come from the diff and not the spec:
- The tree state is recorded in the run file (`skills/subagent-driven-development/scripts/test-run`, the `tree:` line from `git status --porcelain`).
- `task-done` reads "its ledger command back from the run file" (`skills/executing-plans/scripts/task-done`, the awk read of the `command:` entry). The procedure lives in `references/test-run.md`, also from the diff.

B3: PASS
Why: The synopsis says "In SDD, DONE now leads to a controller test run before any review. Failing runs never reach a reviewer," which is a workflow step that now runs differently. It also says "SDD and executing-plans now share one run mechanism and run-file format."

B4: PASS
Contradicted: none
